Hi Frank,

I believe this will just require writing a custom hook.  Hooks handle this output formatting, and are specific to the output device. Um, hooks: http://yihui.name/knitr/hooks are already defined to make customization easier, though your use of centerline{} sounds like a good one.  I guess for some reason it's not possible/desirable to just generate a smaller plot that won't overflow in the first place in your case?

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: Overly wide figures and justification
messages.subject_clean: [knitr] Re: Overly wide figures and justification
messages.body_plain:
In this particular case, I think a quick gsub() should solve the problem, e.g.

\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}
<<setup, include=FALSE>>=
hook_chunk = knit_hooks$get('chunk')
knit_hooks$set(chunk = function(x, options) {
  res = hook_chunk(x, options)
  if (options$fig.align != 'center') return(res)
  gsub('\\{\\\\centering (\\\\includegraphics.+)\n\n\\}',
'\\\\centerline{\\1}', res)
})
@

<<test, fig.height=4, fig.width=8, out.width='6in', fig.align='center'>>=
par(mar=c(4,4,.1,.1))
plot(mpg~wt, data=mtcars)
@
\end{document}

This is hackish, of course. You are recommended to put Rnw and tex
output under version control, so you will be aware of the possible
future changes.

Regards,
Yihui
--

messages.body_plain:
I think most web browsers can tolerate CSS in <body></body>, although
you are supposed to write it in <head></head>.

As replied by Carl in another private thread, you can set the option
'markdown.HTML.stylesheet' for the markdown package, which is called
by knitr to compile markdown vignettes, e.g.
options(markdown.HTML.stylesheet = 'your-own.css').

Yihui

I was hoping to find something that would work across both knitr and pandoc without requiring any changes to the environment:
This way I could pass a long a single file and have it render on someone else's machine without having to include addition files or
commands for them to run.

On a somewhat related note, would it feasible to allow calls to \usepackage within the knitr source file (.Rmd, etc)?

Keep up the good work!

Cheers,
Keith

messages.body_plain:
No, Rmd does not respect \usepackage{}. The only way to do that is a
custom template for Pandoc.

I agree a single file/command will be very useful. I have been
thinking about this problem, and I have an experimental pandoc()
function in knitr, but it is not complete yet. I plan to finish it in
the next version (v1.2). Hopefully you can include the arguments to be
passed to Pandoc in the Rmd file as some "meta data".

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Hmisc summary.formula in html markdown
messages.subject_clean: [knitr] Hmisc summary.formula in html markdown
messages.body_plain:
hmm, that looks tricky to me.  The "table" is being generated by `print.char.matrix`. `print.summary.formula.reverse` passes print.char.matrix a data frame, which you'd probably want to intercept (means hacking the code out of print.summary.formula?) and convert to a table, so that intelligent tools like xtable or pandoc.table (pander package, if you're using pandoc instead of Rstudio/sundown to render markdown) can make some sense of it (e.g. render as an HTML table when you use the chunk option `results="asis"`).  This is probably more robust but more work.

Short of that, note that you can modify the layout a bit my passing the options  like `hsep= '|', csep='|', vsep='-'` to summary.formula (see print.char.matrix documentation), and try and coerce the ascii table to look like something the markdown parser can recognize... e.g. that option should look like a table to pandoc or rstudio...

Here's a whack at that approach, tune as needed.

```{r results="asis"}
library(Hmisc)
df = data.frame(Age = round(rnorm(100, 50,15)), Sex = rep(c("M", "W")))
out <- summary.formula( ~ Age + Sex, data = df, method = "reverse")
print(out, hsep= '|', csep='|', vsep='-', left.border=FALSE, top.border=FALSE)
```

> ```

> Any hints are appreciated, best, hans

messages.subject: custom syntax highlighting
messages.subject_clean: custom syntax highlighting
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm using knitr to write R labs (for teaching intro stat) and in the past I've been able to customize the syntax highlighting using the parser and highlight packages. However, I think because parser is no longer functional, this doesn't work anymore.

Below is a MWE of code I've used in the past (using R 2.15.3, knitr 0.9) that produced the following output (everything looks great):

\documentclass{article}

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
% Packages
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\usepackage[sc]{mathpazo}
%\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}
\usepackage{geometry}
\geometry{verbose,tmargin=2cm,bmargin=2.2cm,lmargin=2.5cm,rmargin=2.5cm}

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
% Redefine colors for syntax highlighting
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\renewcommand{\hlfunctioncall}[1]{\textcolor[rgb]{0.11,0.53,0.93}{\texttt{#1}}}%
\renewcommand{\hlstring}[1]{\textcolor[rgb]{0.65,0.50,0.39}{\texttt{#1}}}%
\renewcommand{\hlsymbol}[1]{\textcolor[rgb]{0.387,0.581,0.148}{\texttt{#1}}}%
\renewcommand{\hlkeyword}[1]{\textcolor[rgb]{0.31,0.65,0.76}{\texttt{#1}}}%
\renewcommand{\hlargument}[1]{\textcolor[rgb]{0.31,0.41,0.53}{\texttt{#1}}}%

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
% Document
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\begin{document}

<<setup, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE>>=
require(parser)
opts_knit$set(use.highlight = TRUE)
@

<<load-data, eval=FALSE>>=
download.file("http://www.openintro.org/stat/data/mlb11.RData", destfile = "mlb11.RData")

load("mlb11.RData")
@

<<cor, eval=FALSE>>=
cor(mlb11$runs, mlb11$at_bats)
@

<<plotss-atbats-runs, eval=FALSE>>=
plot_ss(x = mlb11$at_bats, y = mlb11$runs)
@

\end{document}

 <https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/-Iw48SpTas8A/UYAAy8DdEAI/AAAAAAAAAF4/YVHhJuVosDU/s1600/working.png>
When I try to compile the same document in R3.0 (knitr 1.2), I get an error saying

> Error in library(package="parser", character.only = TRUE)

which makes sense since the parser package seems to no longer work (I've seen some comments about this in past posts as well). Based on past suggestions made on this forum and elsewhere I tried using one of the knitr themes and customizing it.

\documentclass{article}

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
% Packages
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\usepackage[sc]{mathpazo}
%\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}
\usepackage{geometry}
\geometry{verbose,tmargin=2cm,bmargin=2.2cm,lmargin=2.5cm,rmargin=2.5cm}

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
% Document
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\begin{document}

<<setup, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE>>=
thm = structure(list(highlight = "\\definecolor{fgcolor}{rgb}{0, 0, 0}\n
                     \\newcommand{\\hlfunctioncall}[1]{\\textcolor[rgb]{0.11,0.53,0.93}{\\texttt{#1}}}%\n
                     \\newcommand{\\hlstring}[1]{\\textcolor[rgb]{0.65,0.50,0.39}{\\texttt{#1}}}%\n
                     \\newcommand{\\hlsymbol}[1]{\\textcolor[rgb]{0.387,0.581,0.148}{\\texttt{#1}}}%\n
                     \\newcommand{\\hlkeyword}[1]{\\textcolor[rgb]{0.31,0.65,0.76}{\\texttt{#1}}}%\n
                     \\newcommand{\\hlargument}[1]{\\textcolor[rgb]{0.31,0.41,0.53}{\\texttt{#1}}}%\n",
    background = "#f2f2f2", foreground = "#000000"), .Names = c("highlight", "background", "foreground"))
knit_theme$set(thm)
@

<<load-data, eval=FALSE>>=
download.file("http://www.openintro.org/stat/data/mlb11.RData", destfile = "mlb11.RData")

load("mlb11.RData")
@

<<cor, eval=FALSE>>=
cor(mlb11$runs, mlb11$at_bats)
@

<<plotss-atbats-runs, eval=FALSE>>=
plot_ss(x = mlb11$at_bats, y = mlb11$runs)
@

\end{document}

and the result is slightly different:

 <https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/-ci-5ZxAGF1I/UYAEznWne1I/AAAAAAAAAGI/I3N_Up1hqEY/s1600/not+working.png>
The function and the string colors are there, but the symbol, keyword, and argument colors are not being picked up properly.

Any ideas or suggestions would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks,
Mine
